You’ll Never Believe How Much The F15 BMW X5 Now Costs. It’s Pennies on the Dollar!
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
If you want a BMW X5 in your life but don’t fancy the new generation due to its Neue Klasse design inside and out, not to mention the fact that it comes from a minimum of $69,800 (MSRP) in its most basic version, the RWD X5 40, then this would be a good time to search the used car market for an older one.
The G05 can cost between $20,000 and upward of $85,000, depending the mileage, trim level, powertrain, and overall condition. And if you are unfamiliar with the codenames, then you should know that this is the predecessor of the modern-day (G65) Neue Klasse BMW X5. It was made from 2018 to 2026, and it does not show its age yet, this writer thinks.
Is the G05 out of your budget? Then how about its predecessor, the F15 ? This one was made between 2013 and 2018. Production took place not only at the South Carolina factory in USA, but also in Russia, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Egypt. It shared plenty of nuts and bolts with the era’s 5 Series, namely the G30, as well as the old X6 (F16). And it costs between $10,000 and over $40,000 in today’s used car market in USA.
Paying a little over $10,000 would get you an earlier model year, whereas the mid-range model year versions tend to fetch from $15,000 to over $25,000. The range-topping X5 M from this generation generally costs in the region of $20,000, and features a 4.4L twin-turbo V8 with 567 hp (423 kW/575 ps) and 553 lb-ft (750 Nm) of torque, hitting 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.2 seconds.
Photo: Cars&Bids Pictured above is not the X5 M , but an xDrive35i from the 2014 model year. This BMW X5 has 300 horsepower (224 kW/304 ps) and 300 lb-ft (407 Nm) of torque on tap, and power comes from the N55 unit, a 3.0-liter turbocharged straight-six engine. This model uses an eight-speed automatic transmission that sends the output to the xDrive all-wheel drive system, and needed around 6.5 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from zero.
In the North American market, the top speed was electronically limited to 130 mph (210 kph), and overseas market cars could reach 146 mph (235 kph). By the way, Europe’s X5 from this era, in the xDrive35i configuration, had 302 hp (225 kW/306 ps) and 295 lb-ft (400 Nm) of torque to play with.
The pictured BMW X5 had a little over 58,000 miles (~93,400 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. It is presented in Mineral White Metallic on top of an Ivory White interior. The M Sport Package, Driver Assistance Plus Package, Nappa leather upholstery, a panoramic sunroof, power-adjustable front seats with heating and ventilation, a four-zone automatic climate control system, and a Bang & Olufsen premium sound system are mentioned in the ad as being part of the equipment.
Mind you, not everything is perfect, because the SUV in question has chips and scratches on the outside, a scuff on the front bumper, a ding on the tailgate, weathered finish on the exterior trim, and curb rash on the wheels. The wear on the door cards and interior touch points, as well as wear on the front seat bolsters are also mentioned in the ad. Moreover, this ride was involved in two accidents, in August 2021 and January 2024, sustaining “minor” damage in both cases.
Photo: Cars&Bids This BMW X5 has a clean California title. It had its engine oil and filter changed in February 2026, at 57,147 miles (91,969 km), as well as in December 2024, at 50,844 miles (81,825 km). In the latter date, it also had its cabin air filter replaced, the brake fluid flushed, the engine oil filter adapter replaced, and got new spark plugs.
In January 2024, the outside mirror was repaired/replaced, the brake fluid flushed, engine oil and filter changed, rear brake pads and rotors replaced, and tires rotated. The battery was replaced in July 2023, and in November 2022, at 22,675 miles (36,492 km), the SUV had its engine oil and filter changed, and the brake fluid flushed, the listing shows.
According to the ad, the selling dealer reportedly bought this BMW X5 in July 2026, and they recently parted ways with it. The vehicle was accompanied by two keys and nothing else, and it literally went for pennies on the dollar compared to what it initially cost. We don’t know how much the first owner paid for it, but let’s not forget that this model used to retail for over $56,000 back then, and this is a nicely-equipped example with plenty of extras.
The selling price was $11,611, as that’s how much it got at the end of the online auction on Cars&Bids, which concluded on November 13, 2026. The SUV was advertised at no reserve, and you can check it out in more detail here . But before you do, let us know if you would have made it yours for that sum.
